analysis:
The PR is CI-only plus docs and changelog. It touches .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml, docs/developer/build.md and changelog.d/ci-darkbloom-no-github-cache.md. I found no provider runtime, wire protocol, attestation, key, or prefix-cache storage change, so TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-009/TB-011 and T-041 are unaffected in code.

Changed behavior: each routed job (build-cluster, test-cluster, test-cluster-gpu, cluster-release-checks, test-cluster-focused) now starts with a 'Choose this job's Actions cache' step (e.g. lines 794-806, 915-927, 1034-1046, 1203-1215). On a runner named darkbloom-* with no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL it writes CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off to GITHUB_ENV. Cache restore/save steps are gated on env.CI_ACTIONS_CACHE != 'off' (e.g. lines 822, 864, 1055, 1126, 1164, 1224, 1266; audio cache at 576 and 587). This reduces exposure of CI build artifacts to GitHub's shared Actions cache scope, a security improvement.

The 'Discard a damaged or unsafe cached .git' step (lines 831-856 and its copies) now rejects a restored .git that is a symlink, holds symlinks or non-sample hooks, or whose config sets core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or an include. It runs before any git command reads the repository. The cache-poisoning hardening is reasonable. Limits I noticed but did not treat as findings: the config check only inspects files named config/config.worktree, and the git config --file | grep pipeline tolerates errors via '|| true' (fail-open on parse errors). Other dangerous keys such as core.sshCommand, core.pager, filter drivers and credential helpers are not blocked. These are residual hardening gaps in a CI-only control, not regressions, since the base had no such check at all.

Unverified contracts: the plane's DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL behavior, the runner naming darkbloom-<id>, and the other workflows and composite actions (not in this batch) that the docs say are also gated. The doc says scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py enforces the gating; that script was not supplied. The truncated patch excerpt for the workflow was fully covered by the head text for the lines shown.
